question.leadin: Answer some questions about 2011's natural disasters.
question.text: On October 23, 2011 a 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck near Van in the eastern portion of this country. The earthquake was also felt in nearby Armenia and Iran, and tremors reached as far as this country's capital of Ankara.
question.clue: Herodotus, author of the Histories, was native of this modern-day country, as he was born in Halicarnassus.

swap.leadin: This emperor was the son of Selim the Grim.
swap.text: Name this greatest of the Ottoman Emperors who conquered Hungary at the Battle of Mohacs in 1526 and besieged Vienna in 1529.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [accept Suleiman the Lawgiver; accept Suleiman I; prompt on Suleiman]
swap.clue: A principle known as the "circle of justice" guided the legal kanuns which he set up, and he supported the ascension of John Zapolya following one of his military victories.

question.text: This Ottoman sultan and son of Selim the Grim won the battle of Mohacs and was defeated at the Siege of Vienna. He led the Ottomans during the apex of their power.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman I [accept Suleiman the Magnificent or Suleiman the Lawgiver; prompt on Suleiman]
question.clue: He employed Sinan as the chief architect, married Roxelana, and was often called "kanuni."

swap.text: At Piacenza, Alexios I was calling for help against the "Seljuk" variety of these people, who were themselves a subset of their "Ghuzz" variety. A group of "Young" ones rebelled against Sultan Abdul Hamid II in 1908.
swap.clue: The "16 States" popularized by nationalists from this ethnic group include the Ghaznavids.

question.text: The Fatih Mosque and Tiled Kiosk were built during the reign of this Ottoman sultan, who took Constantinople in May 1453 to earn the epithet "Conqueror."
question.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

swap.text: This pirate sailed the Barbary Coast with his brother Aruj before becoming an admiral in the Ottoman navy and defeating the Holy League at the Battle of Preveza. He shares his name with a Holy Roman Emperor killed in the Third Crusade.
swap.clue: He met with Antonio Rincon to negotiate an alliance between his monarch and Francis I, but his force was defeated at the Battle of Preveza by an allied fleet assembled by Pope Paul III in 1538.

question.text: Ottoman Sultan Murad IV bulldozed coffeehouses to prevent these people from conspiring against him. This military force recruited from the Devshirme("dave-SHEER-may") system was abolished under the Tanzimat reforms.
question.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

swap.text: Forces from New Zealand fought alongside those of Australia as part of the "Anzacs" during this disastrous 1916 British campaign in modern-day Turkey in World War I.
swap.clue: Three attempts were made to take Krithia during this campaign after a successful landing at Cape Helles.

question.leadin: Some discussion of this event has been squashed by legislation called "Article 301," which prohibits insulting the Turkish nation.
question.text: Name this event which was begun by the Tehcir Law and saw hundreds of thousands of members of a European ethnic group killed by Turks during a forced relocation.
question.clue: Operation Nemesis was a plot by the revolutionary Dashnak organization to kill perpetrators of this event, and culminated in the deaths of two members of the "triumvirate" of Committee for Union and Progress members who planned it.

swap.leadin: Hayk, the progenitor of these people, is legendarily claimed to be the great-great grandson of Noah and fought against the Babylonian king Bel.
swap.text: Name this ethnic group that settled around Lake Van and Mount Ararat; the Romans and Persians frequently fought over the throne of these people.
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.text: After the Turkish nationalists rallied to defeat the Greeks, Armenians, and French, this new treaty replaced, and returned all of the concessions of, Sevres.
question.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

swap.text: After the final dissolution of the Ottoman Empire, this man led the new nation of Turkey starting in 1922.
swap.answerHtml: Mustafa <u>Kemal</u> <u>Ataturk</u> [accept either underlined portion; or Mustafa Kemal <u>Pasha</u>]
swap.clue: This commander had to relocate to another building due to the stench following the seizure of a city in a 1922 campaign against King Constantine.

question.leadin: Though it was long known as the sick man of Europe, the First World War dealt the Ottoman Empire its final blow.
question.text: Give this title held by the three men who were part of the Committee of Union and Progress and de facto led the Ottoman Empire during the war. That triumvirate of men with this title also ordered the Armenian genocide.
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: The Polish slave and translator Albertus Bobovius compared this institution to a monastery.
swap.text: Name this institution located in the Topkapı palace whose guards were led by the Chief Black Eunuch. Holders of the title of valide, such as Roxelana, were at the top of this institution's hierarchy.
swap.answerHtml: Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Empire [or the Seraglio]
swap.answer: Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Empire
swap.clue: Talking to members of this institution demystifies it per the letters of Mary Wortley Montagu, which also discussed inoculation.

question.text: The Battle of Zenta forced this 1699 treaty. Rifaat Abou-el-Haj noted that Ottomans used "a sort of make- believe" to reconcile serhadd-i mansure with their first major territorial losses, namely Hungary, in this treaty.
question.clue: Its Russian portion was supplemented in the following year by a treaty which transferred Azov, and it exempted an area defined by the Tisza, Mures, and Danube rivers, the Banat of Temesvar, from one provision.

swap.text: In this 1826 event, Sultan Mahmud II had most of the elite Janissaries killed after they revolted at the institution of westernized troops.
swap.clue: The janissaries revolted for a final time in 1826, after which they were finally disbanded in this event that saw most janissary troops executed, exiled, or imprisoned.

question.text: This more famous Ottoman reform was launched in 1839 by Mahmud II. This reform included the abolishment of slavery and a new tax structure, and its name translates as reorganization.
question.clue: This period begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber.

swap.leadin: This treaty intended to create a neutral "Zone of Straits" surrounding the Bospohorus and the Dardanelles, and it called for the Malta Tribunals.
swap.text: Name this 1920 treaty which proposed divisions of Ottoman lands but was never ratified and replaced with the Treaty of Lausanne.
swap.clue: This treaty formalized the territory divisions laid out four months prior at the San Remo Conference, as well the earlier end of hostilities in the Armistice of Mudros.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the decline and fall of the Ottoman Empire. Since Chris Ray apparently doesn't know what questions are, your reader will read these statements with a ridiculous and uncalled-for upwards inflection.
question.text: This period of reform introduced many European concepts of nationality to the empire, including the adoption of a national anthem and the creation of citizenship???
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.leadin: This family included Kara Mustafa Pasha.
swap.text: Name this Turkish noble family who, as grand viziers, presided over the last great era of Ottoman power, including the 1683 Siege of Vienna.
swap.clue: This family of Ottoman viziers, the first of whom served under Sultan Mehmet IV, while another, Kara Mustafa, was strangled on the way back to Istanbul after failing to take Vienna in 1683.
